description:
Ukrainian authorities say Starlink has restricted some military internet services, disrupting operations amid an escalating dispute with the Trump administration.

Ukrainian authorities said they were caught off-guard by restrictions on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink, called Starshield.

Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government and that any limits on its speed or usage are up to the US military and president, SpaceX CEO Musk said on his social media platform X, adding that Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX and is limited to civilian or defensive activities.

Inflation rose faster than expected last month, and more broadly than expected, with price pressures extending well beyond the pump, new Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed Wednesday. 

The latest Consumer Price Index showed that prices rose 0.6% in September from the month before, bringing the annual rate of inflation to 3.7%, up from 3.4% in August and above economists’ expectations for a 3.6% increase. 

CNN Business senior reporter David Goldman breaks down whether President Trump has lived up to his campaign promises on the economy. Also, CNN senior reporter Matt Egan runs through the "disappointing read on inflation."

Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis traded fresh strikes on energy infrastructure, with the Iran-backed group again targeting the Saudi capital and appearing to hit the headquarters of Saudi state oil giant Aramco. 

Saudi authorities said an administrative building belonging to Aramco in the Eastern Province city of Dhahran, where the company is headquartered, was targeted. It caused a limited fire, but it’s unclear whether this was due to a direct hit or falling debris. No injuries were reported. 

CNN's Nic Robertson has the details and CNN's Becky Anderson discusses Houthi military capability with former US State Department official Abbas Dahouk.

author: CNN
description:
The Trump administration must allow CNN, MS NOW, and Politico to access the White House while their lawsuit over the president’s press ban plays out, a federal judge ruled on Tuesday.

US District Judge Tim Kelly said that President Donald Trump’s press ban likely violated the First Amendment, expanding upon his previous legal rationale for ordering that the three outlets be allowed access to the White House. He wrote that Trump’s own comments explaining the ban show a “likely causal link between Plaintiffs’ protected First Amendment speech and his revocation of their hard passes.”

CNN's chairman & editor-in-chief Mark Thompson reacts to the ruling, and CNN chief media analyst Brian Stelter unpacks the judge's decision.

Some conservative voices are saying the Iran war is going in America’s favor: “We won. Iran lost. Period,” says CNN’s Scott Jennings.
